x: Scantlebury was third in the 100 Yards to McDonald Bailey. Len Marchant came second in the 880 Yards, and both these runners represented the R.A.F. in the Inter-Service Championships, where Len Marchant finished third in the 1 Mile, and was also in the winning 4 x 880 team.
McDonald Bailey, the West Indian runner, won the 100 Yards for the Poly, and Jack Frost ran well to gain third place for us. Dicky Dumbrill also ran third in the second race over this distance.

Merrett was our only runner to get placed in the trophy events, when finishing third in the 220 yards to E. McDonald Bailey and Clay Gibbs, both coloured runners, and his was a really sound performance.

A lot, of course, depends on the seeding of the heats, and with such men as McDonald Bailey, Derek Pugh, Arthur Wint, Roger Bannister, to mention only a few who were competing, it will be seen that the class was very, very high.

Basil Walden won his 100 heat in 10.3 secs., and was placed 2nd to McDonald Bailey in the final which was won in 9.8 secs. Bill Lucas ran well to take 3rd place in the 3 miles run with Len Herbert in 6th place, but we had no finalists in the 440.
Denis Merrett and Basil Walden were down as reserves for the 100 yards race, but as McDonald Bailey and Brian Shenton were present, their services were not required.

Dicky Bartlett ran 3rd in the 220 yds., which was won by Brian Shenton, and then came the sensation of the meeting, McDonald Bailey could only finish 3rd in the 100 yds. and was beaten by Ruddy of A.P.M., and our own Ron Holtum in 10.1 secs.
In the 220 yds. we saw Denis Merrett doing 22.3 secs. in his heat, which was won by McDonald Bailey in 21.3 secs., and he thus qualified for the semi-finals.

The following year he startled everybody by defeating the almost invincible "black flash", McDonald Bailey. The positions were reversed a few weeks later in Scotland where, on a grass track, Ron was beaten 9.6 to 9.8 (Unfortunately, not an official A.A.A. time).

He won no less than 7 Berkshire A.A.A. titles at 100, 220 and 440 yards in the early 1950's and was a member of the Polytechnic 4 x 110 and 4 x 440 relay teams which includeded Macdonald Bailey, Arthur Wint and Brian Shenton, and which won A.A.A. titles.

No finer compliment can be paid to our two than to list a handful of previous winners of these titles. 220yds/200m - Eric Liddell, McDonald Bailey, Steve Riddick, Don Quarrie, Mel Lattany and Stanley Floyd.
The new sprint star was McDonald Bailey, probably the first of many world class Caribbean performers. Arthur Wint brought off the difficult 440/880 double prior to his Olympic success.
The principal talking points in early season were the hopes of McDonald Bailey, the Trinidadian born sprinter who had elected to run for Britain and who had shown such good form since 1946.
The first day again showed E. McDonald Bailey to be our outstanding sprinter, winning the invitation 200 metres in 21.3 by five metres and close to the British record.
Britain's MacDonald Bailey ran extremely well for 3rd place in the 100m and 4th in the 200m but did not quite recapture his form of the previous year when he equalled the World 100 metre Record.
